lastCompletedStory.title: Verify the downloaded artifact against SHA256SUMS.txt in install.sh before installing

nextStoryContext: install.sh gained a new '--- Verify: SHA-256 checksum against the release's SHA256SUMS.txt ---' section inserted between the existing 'chmod +x "${TMP_BIN}"' line and the pre-existing '--- Install: additive' comment (so AC1's awk oracle, which requires the literal string SHA256SUMS to textually precede that install-section marker, is satisfied by construction, not by ordering luck). It downloads https://github.com/${REPO}/releases/download/${TAG}/SHA256SUMS.txt to a second mktemp (TMP_SUMS, folded into the same EXIT trap as TMP_BIN so both are cleaned up), greps the manifest for the two-space `<hash>  ${ASSET}` line format that both `shasum -a 256` and GNU `sha256sum` emit in text mode (confirmed identical format cross-platform via Step 5.5 below), and probes `command -v sha256sum` first then falls back to `command -v shasum -a 256` (macOS ships shasum not sha256sum, Linux ships sha256sum and often not shasum -- AC2's oracle just greps both tokens appear in the file, satisfied). Every bare `VAR="$(pipeline)"` capture (the manifest grep+awk, and each hash tool's own capture) is guarded per the CAM-460 set -e/pipefail gotcha already in patterns.md: the manifest lookup uses `|| true` + an explicit -z check (grep-no-match is a legitimate 'no such asset in manifest' outcome, not a hard reachability failure), the two hash-tool captures use `if ! VAR="$(...)"; then <diagnostic>; exit 1; fi` (a hash-tool invocation failing is a harder, less-expected failure). test/install-sh.test.ts's writeFakeCurl gained a third behavior dimension inside its existing 'success'-shaped shim: the fake curl now parses its own argv for BOTH `-o <path>` and the positional URL (previously only `-o` mattered), branches on whether the URL contains SHA256SUMS.txt (manifest call) vs not (asset call), and persists asset-name+digest state in a `.checksum-state` file next to the shim binary itself (`$(dirname "$0")`) since the three curl invocations are three separate subprocesses that can't share bash variables -- the digest is always computed at test-run time from the exact dummy payload bytes the shim just wrote (via a shared `hash_file()` helper that probes sha256sum/shasum exactly like install.sh does), never a frozen hex literal (AC4's negative-grep oracle enforces this). Added behavior='checksum-mismatch' (new describe block) reuses the same shim shape but overrides the manifest digest with `sha256sum of empty stdin` (a real, dynamically-computed-but-guaranteed-different hash, not a hardcoded wrong string) to prove the new verify-before-install gate actually blocks a corrupted download (exit 1, no gateship/gship written) -- this test goes beyond what any AC oracle strictly requires but is the direct regression coverage for the feature this story exists to add, not scope creep into an unrelated area. All 7 ACs verified green individually plus the full spine: typecheck 0 errors, bun test 5999 pass/0 fail, bun run check:all exit 0 (coverage/dead-code/dup/file-size/debt-markers/ci-parity/agents-md/test-sleeps/skip-ratchet all ok, no budget or ignore-list edits needed since neither file crossed any ceiling). Neither file touches vendor/ or templates/, so embed-vendor:check (already part of the spine) needed no extra standalone run.

officialDocsValidated.lib: GNU coreutils sha256sum / macOS shasum (shell checksum tools, not a versioned package)
officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed GNU sha256sum's text-mode manifest line format is '<64-hex-digest>  <filename>' (two literal spaces, the second being the text/binary-mode indicator character), and that macOS shasum -a 256's default (text) mode emits the byte-identical format -- the two tools are deliberately cross-compatible, so a manifest produced by `shasum -a 256` on the macOS release runner (per build-release.sh, US-001) is correctly parsed by either shasum or sha256sum on the installing machine. This confirms install.sh's `grep -F "  ${ASSET}"` (two-space literal) plus `awk '{print $1}'` field extraction is correct against both tool families, with no format-translation needed.
